requirements.requirement: Serve a package repository from local storage on node1
requirements.summary: A flat repo was built at /srv/local-repo/pool with dpkg-scanpackages generating Packages/Packages.gz (cmd-5ee464be0a50461a), initially served via a foreground python3 http.server (cmd-70f1b251047348c4, verified reachable via curl in cmd-5425d934f38341b5), then converted to a persistent systemd unit local-repo-http.service (cmd-49d364fb0aab4b4f, cmd-425187b923a84b96). The initial systemd start conflicted with the still-running foreground process and entered a crash loop (cmd-1ab64ecdd3bf4d5b showed 'failed'), but this was corrected by killing the old process and restarting the unit (cmd-19fac1eee55f4bc4), after which the service was confirmed active and serving Packages (cmd-42d5530a3a6e4c13). The after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms the service listening on 10.100.2.10:8080.

requirements.requirement: Make the usual remote repositories unreachable while installing from the local repo
requirements.summary: Remote reachability was confirmed at baseline (curl 200 for archive.ubuntu.com and security.ubuntu.com, cmd-7de0581fe1fa44a6) before iptables/ip6tables REJECT rules were added for all resolved IPv4/IPv6 addresses of both hosts (cmd-2aaff5f14fcb4821), after which curl to both hosts failed to connect (exit 7) (cmd-6a720ff74443489d). The default apt sources file was additionally disabled and replaced with a local-repo source (cmd-089b92019cc74933), giving both network-level and configuration-level isolation from the remotes during the install.

requirements.requirement: Install a package from the local repository while remotes are unreachable, and confirm it works
requirements.summary: With remotes network-blocked and apt pointed only at the local repo, apt-get update succeeded against the local source after a path-layout fix (cmd-91b04423f8e7494f, cmd-390b6416185f4d8e), then apt-get install -y hello fetched and installed the package solely from http://10.100.2.10:8080 (cmd-7f053f81fcfd4fc0), and running the binary printed the expected 'Hello, world!' output (cmd-55a94536747d4aed).

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task were directly demonstrated: a local flat apt repository was built and served from node1, the remote Ubuntu repositories were made genuinely unreachable via both network-level firewall rules and apt source configuration, and the hello package was installed and verified functional entirely from the local repo while remotes were blocked. The independent, mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also executed with a valid pre-restart baseline, an acknowledged reboot, a changed boot_id, and recovered service/package state post-reboot, though the firewall REJECT rules used to block remotes were not persistent and had reverted to zero after the reboot, which does not affect task satisfaction (reboot persistence of isolation was not part of the contract) but is a limitation of the restart evidence.
limitations: The iptables/ip6tables REJECT rules blocking remote repos were not persisted across reboot (0 rules found post-restart vs 9 pre-restart); post-restart apt isolation relied only on the disabled sources file, not network blocking, which was not directly re-tested against the remotes after reboot.

The post-reboot apt-get update output (cmd-6b33b6dc53824a8b) is truncated/interleaved with a 404 for the optional Translation-en index; the Packages fetch itself was not shown as explicitly succeeding in the truncated stdout, though the preceding hello install already used only Packages before reboot.

No evidence of explicit iptables-persistent/netfilter-persistent installation was captured, so it cannot be confirmed whether the firewall's non-persistence was an oversight or an accepted transient measure.

operational_hygiene.summary: Nearly all state-changing commands map directly to the task: repo construction, apt source changes, and firewall rules were purposeful and retained where required. Two self-inflicted hiccups occurred but were bounded and corrected within the trace: (1) the systemd local-repo-http.service entered a restart-loop (cmd-1ab64ecdd3bf4d5b) because the earlier foreground python3 http.server process was not killed before enabling the unit, fixed by cmd-19fac1eee55f4bc4; (2) an initial apt-get update against the flat repo failed with 404 due to placing Packages under dists/ instead of the repo root (cmd-668397f8095d4058), corrected by cmd-91b04423f8e7494f. Neither left residue. One notable gap: the iptables/ip6tables REJECT rules used to block the remote repos were not made persistent and were gone after the mandated reboot (cmd-a2bf989e41d84a27 shows 0 REJECT rules post-restart, versus 9 pre-restart in cmd-42d5530a3a6e4c13), so the network-level isolation did not survive the restart even though the task itself did not require reboot persistence.
